mintAuthority.summary: JPYSC uses renewable per-minter allowances plus a per-minter destination whitelist. No minter was active at the observation block, but an EOA minter admin can immediately authorize a new allowance and the 3-of-4 owner Safe can rotate both operational gates; UUPS upgrades are separated behind a two-day timelock controlled by another 3-of-4 Safe.

controls.label: JPYSC minter administrator
controls.capDescription: The minter administrator can configure or renew a per-minter allowance once the current allowance is zero; the verified implementation imposes no global issuance ceiling.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, minterAdmin() returned this EOA. Verified source makes configureMinter/removeMinter exclusive to that address and allows any new allowance after the current allowance reaches zero. Complete MinterConfigured/MinterRemoved replay found the two historical operator addresses 0x7e7b8b835b5face8db66ddc28fae589ee7abb647 and 0x03c1dcfbf5aaa334c3a270a5a2b782bcbf1be5fa both removed; direct isMinter and minterAllowance reads returned false and zero for each.

controls.label: JPYSC mint-destination whitelist manager
controls.evidence: whitelistManager() returned this EOA at Ethereum block 25712112. Verified source requires each mint destination to be whitelisted for the calling minter, so this is an independent operational gate but cannot create supply or grant a mint allowance.

controls.label: JPYSC owner and operational-role recovery Safe
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, owner() returned this 3-of-4 Safe. Safe Transaction Service reported version 1.4.1, four owners, no modules, and zero guard. Verified StablecoinV1 lets the owner rotate the minter administrator and mint-destination whitelist manager immediately, so the Safe can authorize a new mint path even though it is deliberately separated from UUPS upgrade authority.

controls.label: JPYSC two-day UUPS upgrade timelock
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, upgradeAuthority() returned this verified TimelockController and getMinDelay() returned 172800 seconds. StablecoinV1 restricts both _authorizeUpgrade and updateUpgradeAuthority to the current upgrade authority, so the token owner cannot bypass the timelock's two-day delay.

controls.label: JPYSC upgrade-governance Safe (timelock proposer/canceller)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, this Safe was 3-of-4, version 1.4.1, with no modules and zero guard. Timelock hasRole checks returned true for its PROPOSER_ROLE and CANCELLER_ROLE; EXECUTOR_ROLE was open to address zero, so anyone may execute a ready operation but only reviewed proposers can schedule one.

sources.label: SBI Shinsei Trust Bank JPYSC terms
SBI Shinsei Trust statutory JPYSC issuance and deposit balances

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, direct role reads and a complete MinterConfigured/MinterRemoved replay established no live minter but a live EOA minter administrator able to issue renewable allowances without a global on-chain cap. Minting also requires a separately managed per-minter destination whitelist. The 3-of-4 owner Safe can rotate both operational roles; UUPS authority is separated behind a 172800-second TimelockController whose sole live proposer is another 3-of-4 Safe. Official terms state that issuance has no upper limit, so economic cap semantics are unbounded. The only public reserve snapshot retrieved is dated 2026-06-30 and the terms disclaim an issuance audit, so no reconciliation cadence is asserted. SBI Shinsei Trust Bank appears on the FSA's licensed trust-bank list and issues JPYSC as the trust-bank instrument described in official product materials, supporting prudential supervision. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: renewable allowances have no global cap, Japan FSA supervises the issuing trust bank, and the lone statutory snapshot is stale versus current supply and is not a recurring independent attestation.
